note: Adapted from Sands' (1972) species-level description of Anenteotermes ateuchestes, originally in English; the species is soldierless and only the alate and worker are treated; measurement tables, figure numbers, synonymy and distribution records are not translated, and numbers in the measurement tables that cannot be recovered owing to OCR damage are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species is close to A. nanus but distinctly smaller, with longer apical mandibular teeth and an indistinct fontanelle. In the alates the short first marginal tooth of the right mandible is a character commonly used to separate this group of species, but this tooth wears more readily than the second, and worn large specimens of A. polyscolus may closely resemble the present species; the pilosity of the head capsule in the present species is uneven and does not form a felt, whereas in A. polyscolus it is very even over most of its range. In the worker the spiny armature of the enteric valve separates A. cnaphorus, A. nanus and A. polyscolus; A. improelatans is larger and has a shorter mixed segment, A. hemerus is much larger, A. improcinctus is smaller with longer apical teeth, and A. cicur has more conspicuous cephalic setae; A. disluctans is difficult to distinguish except by the slightly more swollen anterior tibia.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity fine, short and rather abundant, pale yellow. Postclypeus rather strongly swollen, Pcl/W 0.32, Pcl/Ri 2.07. Apical teeth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.49; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clear of the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio La/Li·Lm 10.89; insertion of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin shorter than that of the second. Anterior tibia hardly swollen, Ti/Tw 4.59, the third apical spur about half the length of the other two spurs, pale and inconspicuous. Overlap of midgut and hindgut about four times the width of the midgut at the origin of the Malpighian tubules; enteric valve seat with two moderately developed opposing lobes and a smaller third endopad, connected by a short neck to the second paunch, lateral in the unopened abdomen; endopads of the enteric valve all contracted, of roughly equal development, the surface merely scaly; membranous wall of the valve with sparse minute spines between and outside the pads.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle oval, flat, about half the size of an ocellus, yellow and conspicuous; central spot short-oval, flat or slightly raised, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark a flat brown crescent; antennae pale brown. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum pale brown, transverse sutures weakly developed; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and sternites pale brown, sternites yellowish white medially, dorsal and ventral spiracles pale; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, the distance to the compound eye about two thirds of their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately swollen, the posterior margin indistinct in outline and broadly evenly rounded, median suture weakly developed. Apical teeth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.54; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clear of the molar prominence in surface view. Pilosity of the head capsule short, dense, uneven, yellowish brown, not forming a felt.
